name: mris_preproc
purpose: Prepare surface-based data for high-level analysis by resampling surface or volume source data to a common subject (usually an average subject) and concatenating them into one file usable by programs such as mri_glmfit.

inputs.statement: Surface measure files per subject, specified via --meas, --is, or --iv alternatives.
A subject list supplied via repeated --s, an fsgd file (--fsgd), or a subject list file (--f).
inputs.quote:
--fsgd fsgdfile
Specify the list of input subjects from the fsgd file.

inputs.statement: For volume input, a volume file and its registration matrix file of the type accepted/created by tkregister2.
inputs.quote: The registration matrix file is of the type accepted/created by tkregister2.

inputs.statement: A target common-space subject and hemisphere (lh or rh) must be given.
inputs.quote:
--target subject
Subject to use as the common-space.

conditions.statement: All subjects must each be specified with their own --s on the command line; --s is for use with --meas.
conditions.quote: All subjects must be specified in this way on the command-line (ie, each with its own --s).

conditions.statement: --is and --iv are alternatives to --meas but still require that a subject list be supplied.
conditions.quote: This is an alternative to using --meas. This still requires that a subject list be supplied.

conditions.statement: For --paired-diff there must be an even number of inputs.
conditions.quote: There must be an even number of inputs.

conditions.statement: When using full paths with --fsgd, subjects must be in the same order as the input surface files.
conditions.quote: which must be in the same order as the --isp
If you want to cache without actually creating an output, then --cache-out-only. You must supply a tmpdir.

steps.statement: Resample surface or volume source data to the surface of the common-space target subject.
steps.quote: resampling surface or volume source data to a common sujbect (usually an average subject)

steps.statement: Concatenate the resampled inputs into one output file.
steps.quote: and then concatenating them into one file

steps.statement: Optionally smooth on the target surface by FWHM mm or by nearest-neighbor iterations.
steps.quote: Smooth the data on the target surface by fwhm mm.

steps.statement: When sampling a volume, sample a fraction of the thickness along the surface normal.
steps.quote: sample a fraction of the thickness along the surface normal

steps.statement: Optionally compute paired differences after concatenation.
steps.quote: After concatenating all the inputs together, create a new output file by computing paired differences

steps.statement: Optionally compute the mean of all inputs after concatenation and possible paired diffs.
steps.quote: After concatenating all the inputs together (and possibly computing paired diffs), compute the mean of all inputs.

exceptions.statement: For ANALYZE and NIFTI formats, spatial dimension may not exceed 32k elements, so reshaping is turned on when these formats are automatically detected.
exceptions.quote: This will not work for ANALYZE and NIFTI formats because they cannot represent a dimension with more than 32k elements.

exceptions.statement: None of the paired diff options will affect caching.
exceptions.quote: None of the paired diff options will affect caching.

outputs.statement: An output file specified with --out containing the concatenated resampled data.
With caching, per-subject data are saved in the subject's surf directory as hemi.cachefile.
outputs.quote: mris_preproc will save the data for each subject, after resampling to the target and smoothing, in the subjects surf directory as hemi.cachefile.

outputs.statement: Output is a volume-encoded surface file, normally with spatial dimension nvertices-by-1-by-1.
outputs.quote: the output volume-encoded surface file will have spatial dimension of nvertices-by-1-by-1

parameters.statement: --projfrac sets the projection fraction for vol2surf and is 0-1, default 0.
--fwhm sets smoothing by FWHM in mm on the target surface; --fwhm-src smooths the source surface instead.
parameters.quote: Smooth the data on the target surface by fwhm mm.

parameters.statement: --surfreg sets the surface registration to the common space; default is sphere.reg.
parameters.quote: Use hemi.SurfReg as the surface registration to the common space. Default is sphere.reg.

parameters.statement: --srcfmt specifies source format when using --is; --meas implies --srcfmt curv.
